wasm/smolmix/internal-dev/headless.js-26-26 (1)
`26-26`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Add bounds validation for the stress test count parameter.** The `count` URL parameter is parsed without validation, allowing negative or excessively large values that could cause the test suite to hang or exhaust memory. Consider clamping to a reasonable range (e.g., 1-500).
🛡️ Proposed fix to add validation ```diff -const STRESS_COUNT = parseInt(params.get("count") || "10", 10); +const STRESS_COUNT = Math.min(500, Math.max(1, parseInt(params.get("count") || "10", 10))); ```

In `@wasm/smolmix/internal-dev/headless.js` at line 26, STRESS_COUNT is parsed from the URL without validation allowing negative/huge values; change the assignment for the STRESS_COUNT constant so the parsed value is validated as a finite integer and clamped into a safe range (e.g., 1–500), falling back to the default (10) if parseInt yields NaN or a non-finite value; update the const STRESS_COUNT initialization in headless.js to perform parseInt, coerce to integer, then clamp with Math.max/Math.min to ensure it always ends up between 1 and 500. ```
wasm/smolmix/internal-dev/index.js-270-350 (1)
`270-350`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Check for existing WebSocket connection before creating a new one.** If the user clicks "Connect" multiple times rapidly, the previous `activeWs` connection may not be properly closed, leading to orphaned connections. Consider checking `if (activeWs && activeWs.readyState !== MixSocket.CLOSED)` and either preventing the new connection or explicitly closing the old one first.
🔌 Proposed fix to prevent orphaned connections ```diff document.getElementById("btn-ws-connect").addEventListener("click", () => { const url = document.getElementById("ws-url").value.trim(); if (!url) { display("WebSocket URL is required", "red"); return; } + + // Close existing connection if still open + if (activeWs && activeWs.readyState !== MixSocket.CLOSED) { + activeWs.close(); + } const statusEl = document.getElementById("ws-status"); ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@wasm/smolmix/internal-dev/index.js` around lines 270 - 350, The click handler for btn-ws-connect can create orphaned sockets if an existing activeWs isn't closed; before instantiating new MixSocket(url) check activeWs and its readyState (use activeWs.readyState !== MixSocket.CLOSED) and either return early to prevent a new connection or call activeWs.close() (and await/handle its onclose) to cleanly tear down the previous connection; update the handler around the creation of new MixSocket to perform this check/close and reset wsSendQueue only after ensuring the prior socket is closed. ```
wasm/smolmix/tests/tests/smoke.spec.mjs-11-28 (1)
`11-28`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Memory leak: console listener not removed on timeout.** If the timeout fires (line 14-18), the `page.on("console", handler)` listener registered at line 20 is never removed. This causes a memory leak when `waitForConsole` times out, as the handler remains attached to the page for its lifetime.
🐛 Proposed fix to remove listener on timeout ```diff function waitForConsole(page, predicate, timeoutMs = 120_000) { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { + function handler(msg) { + if (predicate(msg.text())) { + clearTimeout(timer); + page.removeListener("console", handler); + resolve(msg.text()); + } + } const timer = setTimeout( () => { + page.removeListener("console", handler); reject( new Error(`Timed out waiting for console message (${timeoutMs}ms)`) - ), + ); + }, timeoutMs ); - page.on("console", function handler(msg) { - if (predicate(msg.text())) { - clearTimeout(timer); - page.removeListener("console", handler); - resolve(msg.text()); - } - }); + page.on("console", handler); }); } ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@wasm/smolmix/tests/tests/smoke.spec.mjs` around lines 11 - 28, The waitForConsole function can leak the console listener because when the timeout triggers the registered handler (added via page.on("console", handler) inside waitForConsole) is not removed; update the timeout callback to remove the same handler before rejecting (e.g., call page.removeListener("console", handler) or page.off("console", handler) and clear the timer) so the handler is always cleaned up on timeout and on successful resolve; ensure you reference the existing handler identifier used in waitForConsole. ```

`25-42`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Memory leak: console listener not removed on timeout.** If the timeout fires (line 28-32), the `page.on("console", handler)` listener registered at line 34 is never removed. This causes a memory leak when `waitForConsole` times out.
🐛 Proposed fix to remove listener on timeout ```diff function waitForConsole(page, predicate, timeoutMs) { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { + function handler(msg) { + if (predicate(msg.text())) { + clearTimeout(timer); + page.removeListener("console", handler); + resolve(msg.text()); + } + } const timer = setTimeout( () => { + page.removeListener("console", handler); reject( new Error(`Timed out waiting for console message (${timeoutMs}ms)`) - ), + ); + }, timeoutMs ); - page.on("console", function handler(msg) { - if (predicate(msg.text())) { - clearTimeout(timer); - page.removeListener("console", handler); - resolve(msg.text()); - } - }); + page.on("console", handler); }); } ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@wasm/smolmix/tests/tests/suite.spec.mjs` around lines 25 - 42, The waitForConsole function registers a persistent console listener via page.on("console", handler) but never removes it when the timeout fires; modify the timeout callback to remove the same handler before rejecting (or switch to page.once) so the listener is cleaned up on timeout — ensure the handler identifier used in page.on("console", handler) is in scope for the timeout callback and call page.removeListener("console", handler) (or replace page.on with page.once) before calling reject(new Error(...)) and clearing the timer. ```

I wish I had a bit more time to go through it more thoroughly, but in general I think this is in a pretty good shape. I haven't gone super in-depth for detailed logic checks - I assume our AI friends have dealt with it. speaking of which, I've left some comments in the existing conversations. we might have to fix some additional things there

also I think it might be worth revisiting all the loops where we get data from IPR - should we continue on errors or just bail? we should have some way of protecting ourselves from garbage

Also I think it would be nice if there was some equivalent of a task tracker that makes sure all tasks required by the tunnel are still healthy because if one of them fails, the rest becomes useless
